pagesShown.title: Addition and Subtraction of Decimals — Learn + Practice

sections.topicHeader: TOPIC: ADDITION AND SUBTRACTION OF DECIMALS

miniLesson.description: Boxed section at top-left. Shows the algorithm step-by-step: '17 + 8.53 = □. To add or subtract decimals and whole numbers, rewrite the whole number in decimal form. 17 = 17.00. Then write the problem vertically and line up the decimal points. Add or subtract from right to left.' With a worked example showing 17.00 + 8.53 = 25.53.
miniLesson.value: The child doesn't need a teacher to explain the concept — the mini lesson IS the teacher. Self-contained instruction.

sample.description: Boxed section at top-right. A fully worked sample problem with answer: '12 - 4.47 = □ = 7.53' with multiple-choice showing the MISSING STEP (which operation was used). Answer box shows the correct bubble filled in.
sample.value: Shows not just what the answer is, but HOW to get there. The student can self-check by comparing their process to the sample.

vocabulary.description: Bold-labeled row below the lesson/sample boxes: 'VOCABULARY: decimal, whole number, decimal point, estimate, sum, difference, round'
vocabulary.value: All key terms in one line. The child knows exactly which math words apply to this topic.

memoryTrigger.description: Bold-labeled row: 'MEMORY TRIGGER: To estimate a sum or difference, first round the numbers. For example, 5.8 is about 6.'
memoryTrigger.value: A one-sentence mnemonic/heuristic the child can remember. Not the full lesson — just the hook that recalls the strategy.

practice.description: 4 word problems (multiple choice, A-D or F-J lettering). Real-world contexts: relay race times, walnut weights, soda bottle volumes, missing-number equations.

answerBox.description: Bubble grid at the bottom for recording answers. Standardized test format.
answerBox.carolyngVerdict: REMOVE. She explicitly said to remove the answer box.

testYourself.description: 6 more word problems (items 5-10), continuing the same topic. Slightly harder: total relay times with 3 runners, estimation ('about how many tapes?'), missing-number equations with 3 terms.

superStarSpecial.description: Starred challenge section at bottom: 'Find the rule for this pattern. Then find the next two numbers in the sequence: 2.25, 1.75, 1.25, □, □. Explain your answer on another sheet of paper.' This extends beyond calculation into pattern recognition and mathematical explanation.
superStarSpecial.value: Differentiation. Enrichment for kids who finish fast or need more challenge. The 'explain your answer' part requires mathematical reasoning in words — another ELA crossover.

pageArchitecture.description: The two-page spread follows a 6-section architecture that Carolyng explicitly named and endorsed: (1) Mini Lesson → (2) Sample → (3) Vocabulary → (4) Memory Trigger → (5) Practice → (6) Super Star Special (challenge). This is a SELF-CONTAINED lesson: the page teaches the concept, provides vocabulary, gives a memory hook, walks through a sample, provides practice, and offers extension. No teacher guide required.
pageArchitecture.flow: top-to-bottom: teach → vocab → memorize → practice → assess → extend

selfContainedLesson.description: Unlike the Harcourt worksheets (which require a teacher guide), this workbook puts the LESSON on the same page as the practice. Mini Lesson + Sample + Vocabulary + Memory Trigger = complete instruction without a separate teaching guide.
selfContainedLesson.value: A parent who doesn't know how to do decimal addition can sit down with the child and BOTH learn from the page. Zero prep time.

memoryTrigger.description: A one-sentence mnemonic or heuristic: 'To estimate a sum or difference, first round the numbers. For example, 5.8 is about 6.' Not the full lesson — just the hook that helps recall the strategy later.
memoryTrigger.value: Retention tool. When the child sees a decimal problem next week, the memory trigger fires: 'round first, then add.' This is spaced-repetition-compatible.

superStarSpecial.description: A challenge problem that extends beyond the topic into pattern recognition, mathematical reasoning, or explanation. Always requires 'explain your answer' — the child has to articulate their thinking.
superStarSpecial.value: Built-in differentiation + metacognition. The 'explain' requirement ensures the child isn't just getting the right number — they understand WHY.

realWorldWordProblems.description: Every practice problem uses a real-world context: relay races, walnut harvesting, soda bottles, tape purchases. Not abstract arithmetic.
realWorldWordProblems.value: The child sees math as relevant. The word problems also practice reading comprehension — you have to understand the story to find the math.

overallLayout.structure: sectioned — clear boxes for Mini Lesson and Sample at top, Vocabulary and Memory Trigger as horizontal bars, Practice problems in a 2-column grid, Answer Box at bottom
overallLayout.spacing: standard — clean and efficient but not cramped
overallLayout.visualHierarchy: section labels in bold caps dominate, content text is regular weight

difficulty.complexity: single-topic, multi-skill (computation + estimation + word problems + pattern recognition)
difficulty.scaffolding: high (mini lesson + sample + memory trigger before any practice)

characters: named characters in word problems only (Fidel, Raj, Daria, Keiko, Jim)
appealDrivers: no visual distractions from math content

gaps.name: self-teaching-math-worksheet
gaps.description: A single-page (or two-page) math worksheet that includes ALL of: topic header, mini lesson (worked algorithm), sample problem (worked with explanation), vocabulary row, memory trigger (one-sentence mnemonic), practice problems (word-problem format, multiple choice), and a Super Star Special challenge extension. The page teaches AND assesses — no separate teacher guide needed. Remove bubble answer boxes; use open-response lines instead.

notes: New source — Continental Press 'Get Ahead in Math' Level C, not Harcourt. Carolyng is now pulling from a SECOND publisher, which means she's comparing approaches. She explicitly named the 6-section architecture (mini lesson, sample, vocab, memory trigger, practice, super star special) as what she likes. She also gave a REMOVAL directive: get rid of the answer box (bubble grid). This is the first time she's told us to SUBTRACT a feature rather than add one. The self-contained-lesson pattern is a new product direction for Homa: materials that don't need a teacher guide because the instruction is ON the page.
